answer: In an agent economy, each identity must lock a distinct timber stake of capital on-ledger before participating in rewards. The system treats every new account as a separate garden plot that requires its own foundation; an attacker wanting many Sybils must therefore acquire and lock separate timber for each, paying the full opportunity cost of that capital for the lock period. Standing on the ledge of limited liquidity, multiplying identities quickly exhausts available funds and becomes uneconomical long before any reward is extracted.
